5	// iOS only: the audio *session* is an iOS concept. The fork is a platform fork,
6	// not a version gate — macOS has no AVAudioSession and never will; every body
7	// below is a no-op there so callers never carry an `#if` of their own
8	// (`MicrophonePermission` and `QuickActions.install()` set the shape).
9	#if os(iOS)
10	    import AVFAudio
11	#endif

13	/// The one owner of the audio session, and of `RTCAudioSession` with it.
14	///
15	/// It exists because two parties now want the session active: a camera session
16	/// playing the robot's audio (the app activates it itself, as it always did),
17	/// and a system call framed through LiveCommunicationKit (the *system* activates
18	/// it, and the app must keep its hands off `setActive` for the call's whole
19	/// life). `owner` says whose turn it is; `CameraSession` and
20	/// `RobotCallController` both talk to this type and never to
21	/// `AVAudioSession`/`RTCAudioSession` directly — keeping every
22	/// `RTCAudioSession` mention in this one file is what makes the handover
23	/// auditable.
24	///
25	/// WebRTC runs in manual-audio mode from the first touch (`useManualAudio` in
26	/// `init`, which `CameraSession.start()` reaches before any peer connection can
27	/// exist): libwebrtc no longer activates the session behind the app's back, and
28	/// `isAudioEnabled` is the explicit lever for its audio unit.
29	@MainActor
30	final class MediaAudioSession {
31	    static let shared = MediaAudioSession()
32	
33	    enum Owner: Equatable, Sendable {
34	        /// No camera session is running and no call is active.
35	        case nobody
36	        /// A camera session is playing (and maybe recording); the app activated
37	        /// the session itself, exactly as it did before calls existed.
38	        case app
39	        /// A LiveCommunicationKit call is active; the system owns activation and
40	        /// reports it through the conversation manager's delegate.
41	        case call
42	    }
43	
44	    private(set) var owner: Owner = .nobody
45	
46	    #if os(iOS)
47	        /// The one audio transition in flight, if any — a deactivation retry
48	        /// after a stop, or a reclaim after a call ends. There is never a reason
49	        /// for two: each entry point cancels the previous one first, because a
50	        /// stop()'s retry loop left running would deactivate the session a
51	        /// fresh start just opened.
52	        private var transitionTask: Task<Void, Never>?
53	
54	        private static let log = Logger(
55	            subsystem: "com.alexey1312.ReachyMini", category: "MediaAudioSession"
56	        )
57	
58	        private init() {
59	            RTCAudioSession.sharedInstance().useManualAudio = true
60	        }
61	    #else
62	        private init() {}
63	    #endif
64	
65	    // MARK: - Camera session lifecycle (from CameraSession)
66	
67	    /// A camera session started: configure for two-way audio and, unless a call
68	    /// already owns activation, activate on the app's own authority.
69	    func cameraSessionStarted() {
70	        #if os(iOS)
71	            transitionTask?.cancel()
72	            transitionTask = nil
73	            let session = AVAudioSession.sharedInstance()
74	            try? session.setCategory(.playAndRecord, mode: .videoChat, options: [.defaultToSpeaker])
75	            if owner != .call {
76	                try? session.setActive(true)
77	                owner = .app
78	            }
79	            RTCAudioSession.sharedInstance().isAudioEnabled = true
80	        #endif
81	    }
82	
83	    /// The mirror `cameraSessionStarted()` is owed: leaving the camera used to
84	    /// keep the app holding a record-category session — other apps' audio
85	    /// stayed ducked and the OS went on treating this one as a recorder.
86	    /// `.notifyOthersOnDeactivation` is what lets them resume.
87	    ///
88	    /// Under `.call` this is deliberately a no-op: the system owns activation
89	    /// for the call's whole life, and the deactivation arrives through
90	    /// `callDidDeactivate(_:cameraStillRunning:)` instead.
91	    func cameraSessionStopped() {
92	        #if os(iOS)
93	            guard owner != .call else { return }
94	            RTCAudioSession.sharedInstance().isAudioEnabled = false
95	            guard owner == .app else { return }
96	            owner = .nobody
97	            transitionTask?.cancel()
98	            transitionTask = Task { await Self.releaseAudioSession() }
99	        #endif
100	    }
101	
102	    // MARK: - Call lifecycle (from RobotCallController)
103	
104	    // The whole block is iOS-only, not just the bodies: `AVAudioSession` in a
105	    // *signature* is what does not compile on macOS — the camera methods above
106	    // fork inside because `CameraSession` calls them from cross-platform code,
107	    // while everything below has exactly one caller and it is `#if os(iOS)`
108	    // itself.
109	    #if os(iOS)
110	        /// A call is about to be reported: from here until the call ends the
111	        /// system owns activation, so any in-flight transition of the app's is
112	        /// stale.
113	        func callWillStart() {
114	            transitionTask?.cancel()
115	            transitionTask = nil
116	            owner = .call
117	            // **Take WebRTC's audio unit down on purpose, and this line is the
118	            // whole fix.** The system is about to interrupt this session and
119	            // activate its own — measured: `Session interrupted, will stop
120	            // iounit` lands ~700 ms after the start and `didActivate` ~80 ms
121	            // after that. Turning the flag on again in `callDidActivate` only
122	            // restarts the unit if it is a *change*, and `cameraSessionStarted`
123	            // has already set it `true` for passive listening. Assigning `true`
124	            // to a `true` flag restarts nothing, so #111 shipped a call that
125	            // was silent in both directions while passive audio worked.
126	            RTCAudioSession.sharedInstance().isAudioEnabled = false
127	            Self.log.notice("Call starting; audio handed to the system")
128	        }
129	
130	        /// The system activated the call's audio session — hand it to WebRTC.
131	        /// This is where the audio unit comes back up, and it can only do so
132	        /// because `callWillStart` took it down first.
133	        func callDidActivate(_ session: AVAudioSession) {
134	            let rtc = RTCAudioSession.sharedInstance()
135	            rtc.audioSessionDidActivate(session)
136	            rtc.isAudioEnabled = true
137	            Self.log.notice("System activated the call's session; audio on")
138	        }
139	
140	        /// The call ended and the system deactivated its session. A camera
141	        /// session still running goes back to app ownership (the
142	        /// passive-viewing shape); otherwise audio winds down entirely.
143	        func callDidDeactivate(_ session: AVAudioSession, cameraStillRunning: Bool) {
144	            let rtc = RTCAudioSession.sharedInstance()
145	            rtc.audioSessionDidDeactivate(session)
146	            // Down unconditionally, for the reason `callWillStart` gives: the
147	            // reclaim below has to be able to turn it back *on*.
148	            rtc.isAudioEnabled = false
149	            Self.log.notice(
150	                "System deactivated the call's session; camera running: \(cameraStillRunning, privacy: .public)"
151	            )
152	            guard owner == .call else { return }
153	            if cameraStillRunning {
154	                owner = .app
155	                transitionTask?.cancel()
156	                transitionTask = Task { await Self.reclaimForApp() }
157	            } else {
158	                owner = .nobody
159	            }
160	        }
161	    #endif
162	
163	    #if os(iOS)
164	        /// `setActive(false)` races WebRTC's own audio unit, which winds down on
165	        /// a background thread after the caller has already returned —
166	        /// deactivating immediately commonly fails "session is busy", and a
167	        /// `try?` there made the release silently not happen. So: retry
168	        /// briefly, and log when the OS still refuses, because a swallowed
169	        /// failure looks exactly like the ducked-audio bug this method exists
170	        /// to end.
171	        private static func releaseAudioSession() async {
172	            for _ in 0 ..< 5 {
173	                do {
174	                    try AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().setActive(
175	                        false,
176	                        options: [.notifyOthersOnDeactivation]
177	                    )
178	                    return
179	                } catch {
180	                    guard await (try? Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(200))) != nil else { return }
181	                }
182	            }
183	            log.warning("Audio session would not deactivate; other apps' audio may stay ducked")
184	        }
185	
186	        /// The reverse race, after a call ends with the camera still up: the
187	        /// system has just deactivated the call's session, and re-activating the
188	        /// app's own can briefly refuse while that settles. Same retry shape.
189	        private static func reclaimForApp() async {
190	            for _ in 0 ..< 5 {
191	                do {
192	                    try AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().setActive(true)
193	                    // Passive listening again: the session is the app's, so the
194	                    // audio unit has to be told to come back.
195	                    RTCAudioSession.sharedInstance().isAudioEnabled = true
196	                    return
197	                } catch {
198	                    guard await (try? Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(200))) != nil else { return }
199	                }
200	            }
201	            log.warning("Audio session would not reactivate after the call; robot audio may stay silent")
202	        }
203	    #endif
204	}

4	// A platform fork, not a version gate: LiveCommunicationKit is
5	// `@available(macOS, unavailable)` outright — there is no macOS floor bump that
6	// brings it back, unlike the Control Centre widgets' `#if os(iOS)`. The public
7	// surface below is cross-platform so no caller carries an `#if` of its own; on
8	// macOS every method degrades to the direct microphone toggle this app always
9	// had.
10	#if os(iOS)
11	    @preconcurrency import AVFAudio
12	    @preconcurrency import LiveCommunicationKit
13	    import OSLog
14	    import UIKit
15	#endif

17	/// Frames the two-way WebRTC session as a system call (issue #78): Recents,
18	/// Lock Screen, Dynamic Island — the system call UI only, `CameraSession` keeps
19	/// doing the media work.
20	///
21	/// Every decision lives in `CallLifecycle`, which is tested; this class is the
22	/// adapter over `ConversationManager` and is untested by design — the framework
23	/// only stands up on a device, the same trade `WebRTCDataChannel` documents.
24	///
25	/// The `ConversationManager` is created **lazily on the first call start**,
26	/// never at construction: previews, the snapshot suite and the storybook all
27	/// build the view tree that owns this controller, and registering with the
28	/// system's call service from a snapshot run is exactly the class of side
29	/// effect `CameraSession.deinit`'s guard exists to prevent.
30	@MainActor
31	@Observable
32	public final class RobotCallController {
33	    /// The call the system is currently showing, if any.
34	    public struct ActiveCall: Equatable, Sendable {
35	        /// `RobotIdentity.deduplicationKey` — rule 4, identity never an address.
36	        public let robotID: String
37	        public let robotName: String?
38	    }
39	
40	    public private(set) var activeCall: ActiveCall?
41	
42	    /// Bumped once per started call, after the system accepted it — the moment
43	    /// the start-call intent should be donated. The UI layer watches this and
44	    /// reads `activeCall` for the who.
45	    public private(set) var donationCount = 0
46	
47	    public var hasActiveCall: Bool {
48	        activeCall != nil
49	    }
50	
51	    /// True from the tap that asks for the microphone until the call is over —
52	    /// the window `hasActiveCall` misses, because `activeCall` fills only once the
53	    /// system has handed the start back. Suspending the viewport in that window
54	    /// destroys the `CameraSession` the call is placed over; the reasoning is in
55	    /// `ReachyMedia/AGENTS.md`. `activeCall` stays the answer to *who* is called.
56	    public private(set) var keepsSessionAlive = false
57	
58	    @ObservationIgnored private var currentRobotID: String?
59	    @ObservationIgnored private var currentRobotName: String?
60	
61	    public init() {}
62	
63	    #if DEBUG
64	        /// A controller that reports an active call without touching the system's
65	        /// call service. `activeCall` is otherwise only written from a
66	        /// `ConversationManager` callback, which needs a device — so this is the
67	        /// only way a preview can capture the End button at all.
68	        public static func preview(robotName: String? = nil) -> RobotCallController {
69	            let controller = RobotCallController()
70	            controller.activeCall = ActiveCall(robotID: "preview-robot", robotName: robotName)
71	            return controller
72	        }
73	    #endif
74	
75	    /// Keeps the controller pointed at the connected robot; a robot change under
76	    /// an active call ends the call — the far side of it is gone.
77	    public func robotChanged(id: String?, name: String?) {
78	        currentRobotID = id
79	        currentRobotName = name
80	        #if os(iOS)
81	            if let activeCall, activeCall.robotID != id {
82	                run(lifecycle.handle(.sessionBecameIneligible(.remoteEnded)))
83	            }
84	            // Warm the manager the moment a real robot connects, not at the
85	            // first tap: Apple's guidance is to create it early in the app's
86	            // life, and creating it inside the tap's own start raced the
87	            // system's registration on a device. This path never runs from
88	            // previews or the storybook — `RootCallLifecycle` only calls
89	            // `robotChanged` outside preview mode — so the snapshot-safety
90	            // argument for laziness survives intact.
91	            if id != nil, manager == nil {
92	                _ = ensureManager()
93	            }
94	        #endif
95	    }
96	
97	    /// The mic button's one entry point. On iOS an unmute with no call *is*
98	    /// placing the call; a toggle during one routes through the system so the
99	    /// Lock Screen's mute state stays in step. On macOS there is no system call
100	    /// UI and this is the direct toggle it always was.
101	    public func toggleMic(for session: CameraSession) {
102	        #if os(iOS)
103	            self.session = session
104	            run(lifecycle.handle(session.isMicEnabled ? .muteTapped : .unmuteTapped))
105	        #else
106	            session.setMicEnabled(!session.isMicEnabled)
107	        #endif
108	    }
109	
110	    /// The redial path: a Recents tap or the Siri phrase landed, the stream is
111	    /// up, unmute as if the button had been tapped.
112	    public func startCall(for session: CameraSession) {
113	        #if os(iOS)
114	            guard !session.isMicEnabled else { return }
115	            self.session = session
116	            run(lifecycle.handle(.unmuteTapped))
117	        #else
118	            session.setMicEnabled(true)
119	        #endif
120	    }
121	
122	    /// Ends the call from inside the app — the red button beside the microphone.
123	    /// It exists because ending used to belong to the system UI alone, which iOS
124	    /// does not draw over the app owning the call; `ReachyMedia/AGENTS.md` has it.
125	    public func endCall() {
126	        #if os(iOS)
127	            run(lifecycle.handle(.endTapped))
128	        #endif
129	        // No macOS branch: no call ever becomes active there, so nothing draws.
130	    }
131	
132	    /// The session under the call went away — robot asleep or disconnected,
133	    /// stream failed, viewport target gone. `failed` picks the reason the
134	    /// system shows; a sleeping robot ended the call, it did not fail it.
135	    public func sessionBecameIneligible(failed: Bool) {
136	        #if os(iOS)
137	            run(lifecycle.handle(.sessionBecameIneligible(failed ? .failed : .remoteEnded)))
138	        #endif
139	    }
140	
141	    #if os(iOS)
142	        /// The whole start chain logs here, because it shipped once with every
143	        /// failure swallowed: the system refused the start, nothing was
144	        /// written anywhere, and the mic button read as dead. Read it in
145	        /// Console with subsystem `com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`.
146	        private static let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.alexey1312.ReachyMini", category: "RobotCall")
147	
148	        @ObservationIgnored private var lifecycle = CallLifecycle()
149	        @ObservationIgnored private var manager: ConversationManager?
150	        @ObservationIgnored private var delegateAdapter: ConversationDelegateAdapter?
151	        @ObservationIgnored private weak var session: CameraSession?
152	        /// The system action currently being performed; consumed by the
153	        /// `fulfillPendingAction` / `failPendingAction` effects.
154	        @ObservationIgnored private var pendingSystemAction: ConversationAction?
155	        @ObservationIgnored private var conversationUUID: UUID?
156	        /// Who the in-flight start is calling; promoted to `activeCall` when the
157	        /// system hands the start back to perform.
158	        @ObservationIgnored private var pendingRobot: ActiveCall?
159	
160	        // MARK: - Reducer effects
161	
162	        private func run(_ effects: [CallLifecycle.Effect]) {
163	            for effect in effects {
164	                perform(effect)
165	            }
166	            // Postcondition, not an effect: `activeCall` mirrors the reducer's
167	            // state so the keep-alive and the donation watcher read one truth.
168	            if lifecycle.state != .active {
169	                activeCall = nil
170	                if lifecycle.state == .idle {
171	                    conversationUUID = nil
172	                    pendingRobot = nil
173	                }
174	            }
175	            keepsSessionAlive = lifecycle.state != .idle
176	        }
177	
178	        private func perform(_ effect: CallLifecycle.Effect) {
179	            switch effect {
180	            case .requestMicPermissionThenStart:
181	                requestMicPermissionThenStart()
182	            case let .performMuteAction(isMuted):
183	                performMuteAction(isMuted: isMuted)
184	            case .performEndAction:
185	                performEndAction()
186	            case let .applyMic(enabled):
187	                session?.setMicEnabled(enabled)
188	            case .fulfillPendingAction:
189	                pendingSystemAction?.fulfill()
190	                pendingSystemAction = nil
191	            case .failPendingAction:
192	                pendingSystemAction?.fail()
193	                pendingSystemAction = nil
194	            case .takeAudioOwnership:
195	                MediaAudioSession.shared.callWillStart()
196	            case .donate:
197	                donationCount += 1
198	            // One branch for the three reporting effects: a one-case-per-effect
199	            // funnel walks into SwiftLint's cyclomatic ceiling as the reducer grows.
200	            case .reportStartedConnecting, .reportConnected, .reportEnded:
201	                performReport(effect)
202	            }
203	        }
204	
205	        private func performReport(_ effect: CallLifecycle.Effect) {
206	            switch effect {
207	            case .reportStartedConnecting:
208	                report(.conversationStartedConnecting(Date()))
209	            case .reportConnected:
210	                report(.conversationConnected(Date()))
211	            case let .reportEnded(cause):
212	                Self.log.notice("Ending the call: \(String(describing: cause), privacy: .public)")
213	                report(.conversationEnded(Date(), cause == .failed ? .failed : .remoteEnded))
214	            default:
215	                break
216	            }
217	        }
218	
219	        private func requestMicPermissionThenStart() {
220	            Task { @MainActor in
221	                let permission = await MicrophonePermission.request()
222	                guard permission == .granted else {
223	                    Self.log.notice("Start abandoned: microphone permission refused")
224	                    // Surfaces the existing blocked-button state on the viewport.
225	                    session?.refreshMicPermission()
226	                    run(lifecycle.handle(.micPermissionDenied))
227	                    return
228	                }
229	                await performStart()
230	            }
231	        }
232	
233	        private func performStart() async {
234	            guard let robotID = currentRobotID else {
235	                Self.log.error("Start failed: no connected robot identity to call")
236	                run(lifecycle.handle(.startFailed))
237	                return
238	            }
239	            let uuid = UUID()
240	            conversationUUID = uuid
241	            pendingRobot = ActiveCall(robotID: robotID, robotName: currentRobotName)
242	            // The name, because the call history renders `Handle.value` verbatim
243	            // and nothing else — `AGENTS.md` has what else was tried.
244	            let handle = Handle(type: .generic, value: currentRobotName ?? robotID, displayName: currentRobotName)
245	            let action = StartConversationAction(conversationUUID: uuid, handles: [handle], isVideo: true)
246	            // `.notice`, not `.debug`: the log store drops debug by default, so
247	            // the one line saying a start was attempted was unreadable in the
248	            // field report this logging exists for.
249	            Self.log.notice("Performing StartConversationAction \(uuid, privacy: .public)")
250	            do {
251	                try await ensureManager().perform([action])
252	            } catch {
253	                Self.log.error("""
254	                The system refused the start: \(String(describing: error), privacy: .public) — \
255	                falling back to the bare microphone
256	                """)
257	                run(lifecycle.handle(.startFailed))
258	            }
259	        }
260	
261	        private func performMuteAction(isMuted: Bool) {
262	            guard let uuid = conversationUUID else { return }
263	            let action = MuteConversationAction(conversationUUID: uuid, isMuted: isMuted)
264	            Self.log.notice("Requesting mute isMuted=\(isMuted, privacy: .public) on \(uuid, privacy: .public)")
265	            Task { @MainActor in
266	                do {
267	                    try await ensureManager().perform([action])
268	                } catch {
269	                    Self.log.warning(
270	                        "Mute action refused: \(String(describing: error), privacy: .public)"
271	                    )
272	                }
273	            }
274	        }
275	
276	        /// The mirror of `performMuteAction`, and it owes the lesson #112 left
277	        /// behind: a refusal that goes nowhere is a button that does nothing.
278	        /// If the system will not take the end, close the call here rather than
279	        /// leave somebody tapping a dead control.
280	        private func performEndAction() {
281	            guard let uuid = conversationUUID else { return }
282	            let action = EndConversationAction(conversationUUID: uuid)
283	            Self.log.notice("Requesting end on \(uuid, privacy: .public)")
284	            Task { @MainActor in
285	                do {
286	                    try await ensureManager().perform([action])
287	                } catch {
288	                    let reason = String(describing: error)
289	                    Self.log.error("The system refused the end: \(reason, privacy: .public); closing locally")
290	                    run(lifecycle.handle(.sessionBecameIneligible(.remoteEnded)))
291	                }
292	            }
293	        }
294	
295	        private func report(_ event: Conversation.Event) {
296	            guard let manager, let uuid = conversationUUID,
297	                  let conversation = manager.conversations.first(where: { $0.uuid == uuid })
298	            else { return }
299	            manager.reportConversationEvent(event, for: conversation)
300	        }
301	
302	        // MARK: - Delegate arrivals (hopped to the main actor by the adapter)
303	
304	        // Package-internal, not `fileprivate`: the adapter is a file of its own now.
305	
306	        func handle(action: ConversationAction) {
307	            pendingSystemAction = action
308	            let effects: [CallLifecycle.Effect] = switch action {
309	            case is StartConversationAction:
310	                lifecycle.handle(.performedStart)
311	            case let mute as MuteConversationAction:
312	                lifecycle.handle(.performedMute(isMuted: mute.isMuted))
313	            case is EndConversationAction:
314	                lifecycle.handle(.performedEnd)
315	            default:
316	                refuseUnexpected(action)
317	            }
318	            run(effects)
319	            // The success path wrote nothing at all, so a call that started and
320	            // died seconds later left no trace anywhere.
321	            let performed = Self.describe(action)
322	            let state = String(describing: lifecycle.state)
323	            Self.log.notice("Performed \(performed, privacy: .public); the call is now \(state, privacy: .public)")
324	            if lifecycle.state == .active, activeCall == nil {
325	                activeCall = pendingRobot
326	            }
327	            // An action the reducer neither fulfilled nor failed would hang the
328	            // system UI until its timeout; there is no such path, but the slot
329	            // must not leak an action into the next arrival either way.
330	            pendingSystemAction = nil
331	        }
332	
333	        /// Join/merge/pause never arrive for an outgoing-only app; refuse
334	        /// anything unrecognised rather than leave it to time out.
335	        private func refuseUnexpected(_ action: ConversationAction) -> [CallLifecycle.Effect] {
336	            Self.log.warning(
337	                "Refusing unexpected action \(String(describing: type(of: action)), privacy: .public)"
338	            )
339	            return [.failPendingAction]
340	        }
341	
342	        /// A mute arrives twice per tap; without `isMuted` a duplicate delivery
343	        /// and an echo of the app's own request read identically in the log.
344	        private static func describe(_ action: ConversationAction) -> String {
345	            guard let mute = action as? MuteConversationAction else {
346	                return String(describing: type(of: action))
347	            }
348	            return "MuteConversationAction(isMuted: \(mute.isMuted))"
349	        }
350	
351	        func handleTimeout(of action: ConversationAction) {
352	            Self.log.error("Action timed out: \(Self.describe(action), privacy: .public)")
353	            if action is StartConversationAction {
354	                run(lifecycle.handle(.startFailed))
355	            }
356	            action.fail()
357	        }
358	
359	        func handleManagerReset() {
360	            Self.log.warning("Conversation manager reset")
361	            run(lifecycle.handle(.managerReset))
362	        }
363	
364	        func handleAudioActivated(_ audioSession: AVAudioSession) {
365	            MediaAudioSession.shared.callDidActivate(audioSession)
366	        }
367	
368	        func handleAudioDeactivated(_ audioSession: AVAudioSession) {
369	            MediaAudioSession.shared.callDidDeactivate(
370	                audioSession,
371	                cameraStillRunning: session?.isRunning ?? false
372	            )
373	        }
374	
375	        // MARK: - The manager
376	
377	        private func ensureManager() -> ConversationManager {
378	            if let manager {

Now I understand the full data flow. Let me confirm the entry paths and formalize the finding.

The Handle.value in `StartConversationAction` populates the LiveCommunicationKit-system Recents entry with the robot's **name** (previously the dedupKey). When that Recents entry is tapped, iOS wraps it in an `INStartCallIntent` activity where `personHandle.value` == the robot's name. `CallActivity.robotID(from:)` returns `customIdentifier ?? personHandle?.value` — for a LCK-originated Recents tap, `customIdentifier` isn't set, so the returned "robotID" is actually the robot's user-facing name.

This flows into `CallRequestRouting.decide` as `requestRobotID`, and the new second guard clause (`requestRobotID != connectedRobotName`) is what makes that resolve to `.proceed` and open the microphone.

Security implications:
- `RobotIdentity.name` comes from `GET /api/daemon/robot-name` — the robot itself declares this string, and it is not a stable identity (that's `hardwareID`).
- Names are user-mutable and can collide across robots. A Recents entry labeled "Kitchen" (originally donated by robot A with hardware id X) now matches ANY currently-connected robot whose `.name` equals "Kitchen" — including robot B (hardware id Y) that has been renamed, or a different unit that happens to share that name.
- The routing gate's explicit purpose is documented in the file: "never opens the microphone at a robot the user did not name." The widened matcher relaxes that promise to a non-unique display string.
- Impact: a Recents redial can open the two-way microphone at a robot other than the one whose call created the Recents row. On BLE-discoverable robots where the robot declares its own name, a robot claiming a common name can inherit any user's redial.

The other changes (audio-unit toggle in `MediaAudioSession`, log lines) don't touch sinks with attacker-influenced data — the logged `cameraStillRunning` is a local Bool and the notice strings are static.

findings.explanation: CallRequestRouting.decide is the gate that decides whether an inbound call request opens the microphone at the currently-connected robot. It previously required an exact match on RobotIdentity.deduplicationKey (a stable hardware id). The change widens the accept criterion to ALSO match on RobotIdentity.name — a user-facing display string that (a) comes from GET /api/daemon/robot-name and is therefore chosen by the robot itself, (b) is user-mutable, and (c) is not required to be unique across robots. Because RobotCallController now sets `Handle(type: .generic, value: currentRobotName ?? robotID, …)`, the LCK-system Recents row records the robot's name as its identifier; a tap on that Recents row reaches the app via onContinueUserActivity as an INStartCallIntent whose personHandle.value is that name (customIdentifier is unset for LCK-originated entries — CallActivity.robotID returns personHandle.value). That name string then flows to decide() as requestRobotID and, with the new disjunct, resolves to .proceed → router.tab = .live → call.startCall(for: camera), which unmutes the microphone at whatever robot is currently connected — not necessarily the robot the Recents entry was created for. Concretely: (1) user creates a Recents row while connected to robot A (hardware id X) named 'Kitchen'; later the user is connected to a different robot B (hardware id Y) that has been renamed to 'Kitchen' (or a second unit with the same default name); tapping the old Recents 'Kitchen' silently opens the live microphone at robot B. (2) On BLE discovery a rogue robot that claims a common name inherits any user's redial for that name even though the deduplicationKey (hardwareID) does not match. The routing file's own docstring states the invariant this widening breaks: 'an inbound request … never opens the microphone at a robot the user did not name.' The widened matcher accepts a non-unique, mutable, robot-declared string as sufficient proof of intent.
findings.fix: Do not treat robot name as an identity for authorization. Keep decide() matching only on the stable deduplicationKey. If LCK-Recents redials must be honoured, plumb the deduplicationKey through the Handle by using a distinguishing value (e.g. value: robotID with displayName: currentRobotName, or embed the dedupKey in a structured value the app parses back) rather than putting the display name in Handle.value. Alternatively, when the request comes in via personHandle.value (name), require an additional confirmation (Live-tab-only, no auto-unmute) rather than treating a name match as .proceed.
